fields.name: selected_placement
fields.description: During the video cycle, follow the cube named in the instruction and count completed releases onto purple circular targets chronologically. Count a release only once; ignore pauses, approaches, pickups, button presses, and releases onto bare table. Use surrounding video frames to distinguish a release from a pickup. Write an ordered list beginning with the earliest shown frame where the released cube and withdrawing hand identify the target of the requested ordinal. Track that physical target through the remainder of the video, including after the cube is returned to bare table. For each subsequent motion interval of that target, append the last shown frame before the interval, every shown frame during it, and the first shown frame establishing its settled destination. Use surrounding frames to establish when motion has ended. Keep labels chronological and omit duplicates. Track identity by continuous motion, not nearest final location or spatial rank. If the target never subsequently moves, write only the release frame in a one-element list. If no qualifying placement is identifiable, write an empty list. On every act cycle copy the entire incoming list unchanged; do not replace it with execution frames or a later demonstrated placement. e.g. ["V192"]
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, identify completed placements of the instructed cube onto purple circular targets in chronological order. Count each release onto a target once, not approach frames, pauses, button presses, pickups, or the final release on bare table. Select the placement with the ordinal requested by the instruction. Store an ordered list beginning with the earliest shown frame in which the cube has been released on that target and the withdrawing hand makes the placement identifiable. Track that physical target through the remainder of the demonstration, including after the cube is returned to bare table. For each subsequent motion interval of that target, append the last shown frame before the interval, every shown frame during it, and the first shown frame establishing its settled destination. Use surrounding frames to establish when motion has ended. Keep labels chronological and omit duplicates. Determine identity by continuous motion, not nearest final location or spatial rank. If the target never subsequently moves, store only the release frame in a one-element list. If no qualifying placement can be identified, use an empty list. Fill the list at the video cycle and retain it unchanged throughout execution. e.g. ["V192"]

action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution begins with the gripper open above the table. Use selected_placement to identify the destination physical purple ring. Identify the ring supporting the instructed cube in the first retained frame, then follow that ring's continuous motion through the remaining retained frames to its settled destination. Match that destination to the current scene using the fixed camera and surrounding target layout. If the list contains only the release frame, match directly from that frame. The requested ordinal identifies a placement event and its physical ring, not a fixed tabletop location or the cube's final demonstration location. Use the selected ring's current center for transfer, descent, and retreat. Do not reproduce the demonstration's target exchanges. Do not reproduce the demonstration's button press or its other placements. Manipulate only the instructed color.

Estimate world positions with the calibrated cameras rather than image left/right guesses. Intersect target-center rays with the tabletop plane z=0. Estimate cube horizontal center using its top face at approximately z=0.04, or its footprint at table height; do not project an elevated cube center onto the tabletop. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. World +y is image right in the front camera. Set the hand vertically downward, roll pi (equivalently -pi), pitch zero, and choose yaw aligned with the cube's horizontal edges, choosing the equivalent grasp angle nearest zero. Preserve this grasp orientation while carrying and releasing.

Apply these state-dependent rules. With an open hand and the instructed cube resting away from its destination, if the hand is not already at a pickup hover, command the cube's horizontal center at z=0.15 with gripper open. If the open hand is at that hover, within approximately 1.5 cm horizontally and 1 cm vertically, descend to the visually estimated cube center at z=0.02 and close the gripper. Correct horizontal alignment from the images rather than treating the reported TCP position as the exact previous command.

With the cube held between closed fingers near table height, lift vertically over its current horizontal center to z=0.15, keeping closed. Do not transfer sideways before lifting. With the held cube at z approximately 0.15 and not over the selected target, command the selected target center at z=0.15, keeping closed. With the held cube at hover height over that target, descend to the target center at z=0.005 and open. Treat the usual several-millimetre tracking error as arrival; do not insert unnecessary correction waypoints. With the hand open near the target and the cube released there, retract to the same target center at z=0.15 with the gripper open. This retreat applies even when the wrist or fingers partially obscure the resting cube; use the visible ring, open fingers, and current motion frames to recognize the release.

If perception is ambiguous, use the retained placement and target-motion frames together with both current views to resolve the selected ring's identity and current position before moving toward it. If the cube was not grasped, apply the open-hand pickup rules again using its observed location. If no rule is applicable because the hand occludes the relevant objects, move vertically to a clear z=0.15 observation pose, preserving the gripper state and any held cube, then reassess. Never guess a different target from its ordinal's spatial rank. Do not wait without a visible settling-related purpose, and never command a waypoint identical to the current TCP; any necessary gripper-only change must include at least 2 mm of safe motion.
